Hello, I want to move some of my assets to Bitcoin but I got a question about core protocol security that keeps me away from doing it.

Can government bribe or somehow control core developers to implement a backdoor that gives them ability to create bitcoins out of thin air? Is core protocol security dependent on developers?

Well the code's open source and heavily scrutinized. If an adversary did coerce the developers into adding malicious code they would still need to convince the majority of miners to run it, otherwise miners would just reject the malformed blocks when they don't conform to the protocol specification. Miners have a self interest in keeping bitcoins scarce, they don't want to see their existing coins decrease in value. So they watch out for stuff like this.

Responding to a person on Twitter who said it was "sad" that developer Turn 10 was adding microtransactions to Forza 6, Greenawalt explained the game was "designed, tuned, and tested 100 percent without them." Not only that, but he pointed out that they can be toggled off.

Meh. It's just the tokens which I've ignored since forza 4. I haven't bought 6 yet, but i would have no problem with the tokens if they are implemented the same. For me Forza is all about racing particular tracks and improving my own times. I've actually enjoyed the pacing of getting new cars, and don't see the need for buying tokens to hurry it up. Now if you need a token to access tracks I wouldn't be a happy camper
Yeah, I think they've done a good job of making sure it doesn't impact regular gameplay.

Meanwhile, they've been selling car packs since the dawn of time, and nobody bats an eye about that. If you actually wanted "all" of forza 5 (including the "extra" content that is actually on the disc, but paywalled), you'd be spending hundreds of dollars. People are acting like their behaviour has suddenly become nefarious, but it has always been pretty scummy.

I think that's the bigger issue, for sure. Access to the full game (with all season's car packs) is usually $99, up from the base game's $60. I don't mind the cost because I sink a lot of time into Forza, but it's up to the consumer to decide if the base game offers enough content to warrant $60, and if the $99 for the game + car packs is worth the extra cost. I do think that's a better approach than integrating microtransactions into a game, but the microtransactions I've encountered have been as optional as they come; I haven't spent money on them and it doesn't seem to affect my experience with the game.

Edit: it's a lot like Call of Duty with its season pass DLC. If I don't feel like the base game is worth the price, I won't buy the base game. But if I do feel it's worth it, I might decide that the season pass content is worth the additional cost as well.
